sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The trail now reaches all three blocks. Current order: N-Red-Blue.
Bottom panel shows: Red-N-Blue.
I need to swap N and Red to match the target order.
Key insight from earlier: blocks only move when the trail is touching them. When trail touches blocks, they move at 1x player speed. When not touched, they don't move.
To swap N and Red:
1. Move UP so trail no longer touches any blocks (trail moves faster than blocks)
2. Move DOWN to position trail to touch only Red (not N)
3. Move Red left past N
4. Extend trail to touch all three
But all blocks are on the same row (19-22). The trail is 2 rows tall. I can't touch Red without touching N if they're on the same row.
Wait - let me reconsider. When I move UP, the trail moves 6 rows and touched blocks move 6 rows (1x speed). So the relative vertical position stays the same. The trail will always touch the same blocks.
But earlier, when I moved UP from a state where trail touched N/Red but not Blue, the trail ended up touching all three. That's because Blue was at a different row and the trail moved to overlap with it.
So the key is: I need to first separate the blocks vertically, then I can control them independently.
Plan:
1. Move UP so trail no longer touches blocks (trail moves 6 up, blocks move 6 up -> relative position unchanged, so this doesn't work)
Hmm, the trail and blocks move at the same speed when touched. So I can't change the relative vertical position by moving UP/DOWN.
But earlier, when the trail was touching N/Red but not Blue, moving UP made the trail touch Blue too. That's because Blue was at a different vertical position and didn't move (not touched), while the trail moved up.
So the trick is: if I can make the trail touch only some blocks, those blocks move with the trail while the others stay put. This changes the relative vertical positions.
Current state: trail touches all three blocks (all at rows 19-22).
If I move UP: trail moves 6 up, all blocks move 6 up. Relative positions unchanged. Trail still touches all three.
If I move DOWN: same thing.
So I'm stuck with all three blocks on the same row, all touched by the trail. I can't separate them vertically.
But wait - what if I use LEFT to retract the trail? When the trail retracts, it might no longer touch some blocks.
Currently: trail extends from player (col ~14) to Blue (col ~45).
If I press LEFT, the trail retracts and blocks move left.
After 1 LEFT: trail retracts, blocks move left by 6 cols.
After enough LEFTs, the trail might no longer touch the rightmost block (Blue).
Let me try pressing LEFT multiple times to see when blocks stop being touched.

# Try retracting trail with LEFT to lose contact with some blocks

nodes = seg['nodes']

print(f"Current blocks: {[(n['color'], n['boundary']) for n in blocks]}")

ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')

# Try LEFT to retract trail - see what happens
